data.content_ref: inline:{"analogy":null,"claim":"The single expert remains superior because checklists impose a 'Cognitive Ceiling' that filters out the 'out-of-distribution' anomalies essential for high-reliability judgments in complex tasks.","counterconditions":[{"case":"The task is purely algorithmic and contains no 'out-of-distribution' risks.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"The expert's intuition is heavily corrupted by confirmation bias, making them less likely to see even the 'known' errors listed on the checklist.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"Checklists are closed-set systems; they only capture known failure modes. Expertise is the ability to detect 'unknown unknowns' (out-of-distribution anomalies). Reliability gain in the panel is an illusion caused by a narrow definition of 'reliability' that only counts known-error detection.","premises":[],"schema":"deepreason-reasoning-envelope-v1","scope":{"covers":[],"excludes":[]},"simulation_refs":[],"uncertainties":[]}
